title: Late-stage functionalization with strain-release warheads enables tunable covalent inhibition.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC core record (isOpenAccess=N, inPMC=N, hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, no database cross-references, no text-mined accessions); paper_context.py found zero accessions, zero NCBI links, zero Zenodo/Dryad hits; Zenodo API search on 'adx7219' returned 0 records; PRIDE (proteomics repository) keyword search returned an empty list; MassIVE API returned HTTP 400; the publisher's supplementary PDF and article page both returned HTTP 403; the CCDC (Cambridge crystal structure database) DOI search page is JavaScript-only and exposed no deposition numbers.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the chemistry and the measurements: that the authors made sulfonyl- and sulfonimidoyl-bicyclobutane covalent reactive groups (strained three-dimensional electrophiles that react by releasing ring strain), that these show complete selectivity for cysteine, that they were installed into FDA-approved covalent inhibitors as acrylamide replacements, and that mouse studies were done. This all comes from the 150-word abstract; no figure, table or methods text was retrievable.

a1_downloadable.note: No data file of any kind is obtainable. The article is subscription-only with no PubMed Central copy, the publisher's supplementary-materials PDF returns HTTP 403, and searches of Zenodo, Dryad, PRIDE, MassIVE, NCBI and Europe PMC's accession index all returned nothing. There is no deposited dataset to open.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked against files because none exist, but by construction the reactivity numbers (glutathione half-life, inactivation rate constants, IC50 values) in a synthetic-chemistry paper of this type live inside figures and a supplementary PDF of experimental procedures, not in a column of a machine-readable table. Structures would have to be hand-drawn into SMILES strings.

a3_inputs_present.note: No SMILES strings (text representations of chemical structures) or any other machine-readable molecular input is available; compounds are named and drawn in figures only, which would mean manual transcription of every molecule.

a4_units_stated.note: Not verifiable, but Science-level chemistry supplements normally state units for kinetic measurements. Marked pass only to avoid double-counting; the project is already dead at A1.

a5_enough_rows.note: No row count verified. A single methodology paper of this kind typically reports tens of compounds with reactivity measurements, far under the ~1,500 labelled rows needed for regression or ~400 for classification. I did not see a count anywhere, so this is an expectation, not a measurement.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Small-molecule kinetics tables are tiny; size was never the problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot compare counts: there is no download to compare against the paper, and the paper's full text is not retrievable either.

a8_label_provenance.note: The intended label (measured reaction rate or half-life of a warhead with a thiol) would be a real physical measurement, not another model's output — the one Part A item this paper would clearly have satisfied.

existing_models.name: BIreactive (Boehringer Ingelheim machine-learning model of covalent warhead reactivity, J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2020)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved beyond the abstract-level description: it predicts quantum-chemical activation barriers for acrylamides and 2-chloroacetamides. No split or error metric verified.

existing_models.name: QM/ML acrylamide reactivity model (quantum-mechanics descriptors plus machine learning, J. Comput. Aided Mol. Des. 2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: Search snippet states it outperforms linear regression and structure-based machine-learning models and generalises to unseen acrylamide scaffolds; no number verified.

existing_models.name: Electrophilicity-index / electron-affinity single-parameter models for thiol reactivity (J. Comput. Aided Mol. Des. 2020; ChemRxiv 2025 on N-heteroaryl methylene lactams)
existing_models.score_and_split: Described as robust single-descriptor predictors of covalent reactive group reactivity with thiols, with literature test sets; no number verified.

backbone.name: ChemBERTa (a language model trained on chemical structure strings)
backbone.hardware: laptop CPU would be ample for tens-to-thousands of small molecules

integration.partner_dataset: ChEMBL / PubChem bioactivity, joinable on InChIKey, plus CovPDB (curated covalent protein-ligand co-crystal structures)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Would be: does a warhead's intrinsic reactivity with free thiol predict its selectivity across the measured proteome — but it cannot be asked here because no structures or measurements are machine-readable.

controls.positive_control: None available: with no data file, the textbook check (acrylamides being less reactive than chloroacetamides) cannot be run.
controls.negative_control: Not applicable — no dataset to shuffle labels on.
controls.external_validation: Published thiol-reactivity compilations exist (the acrylamide and lactam series used by the QM/ML papers), but there is nothing in this paper to validate against them.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: with the article paywalled, the supplement returning HTTP 403 and no repository deposit anywhere, there is no measurement series to model.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a molecule's chemical structure to predict how fast its reactive group attaches to a cysteine in a protein.
plain_idea.train_on: Would have been one row per synthesised warhead: its chemical structure plus the reaction conditions. Number of examples: unknown — no table was obtainable, and tens rather than thousands is the realistic expectation for one methodology paper.
plain_idea.predict: Would have been the measured reactivity: half-life of reaction with glutathione (a small thiol used as a stand-in for protein cysteines) or the inactivation rate constant, measured by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry or an enzyme activity assay.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Medicinal chemists tuning covalent drugs want to dial reactivity up or down without resynthesising a series; a reactivity predictor for strained three-dimensional warheads would be genuinely new, since published models cover only flat acrylamides and chloroacetamides.

more_or_better_data.why: We have no data at all — no row count, no file. The existing models (BIreactive, the 2024 QM/ML acrylamide model) at least have published training sets; this paper contributes an unknown, almost certainly small, number of measurements locked in a paywalled PDF.

confidence_score.why: No replicate measurements or per-group counts are visible, so per-prediction uncertainty could not be calibrated even if the numbers were transcribed by hand.

models_beatable.why: BIreactive (2020) is closed-weights industry software and the electrophilicity-index models are single-descriptor fits, so the field is not saturated with open reproducible tools — but that opening cannot be exploited without data.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails every condition: no baseline can be run on this paper's compounds, there is no feature table, and the strain-release warheads here are a different chemotype measured in a different assay from the published acrylamide sets, so the labels are not comparable.

ml_idea: Predict thiol reactivity (glutathione half-life or inactivation rate) of strain-release bicyclobutane warheads from structure using a frozen chemical language model plus a small regression head, then test whether reactivity predicts proteome-wide selectivity. Not executable: the paper publishes no machine-readable structures or measurements.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: there is no dataset to size. If the supplementary tables were ever obtainable, hand-transcribing structures to SMILES would dominate the effort, not compute.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Try to fetch the supplementary materials — done, HTTP 403 — and search every repository for a deposit — done, zero hits. That took five minutes and killed it.

verdict_reason: A1 fails outright: paywalled Science article with no PubMed Central copy, supplement returns HTTP 403, and no deposit in Zenodo, Dryad, PRIDE, MassIVE or NCBI. Even as described, the reactivity data would be tens of compounds inside a procedures PDF, not a labelled table.
